title: Factor Analysis
interviewAnswer: Factor analysis models observed variables as linear combinations of a smaller number of latent factors plus variable-specific noise, focusing on shared covariance structure.
why: Factor analysis is a classic latent-variable model distinct from PCA.
intuition: Several measured variables may move together because of a smaller hidden cause, while each retains its own measurement noise.
deepDive: The model x=Λz+ε assumes latent factors z and diagonal/specific noise ε; maximum-likelihood or Bayesian methods estimate loadings and uncertainty.
commonMistakes: Calling factor analysis identical to PCA.
Interpreting rotated factors as uniquely determined truths.
production: Use domain interpretation and stability checks; latent factors can be non-identifiable up to rotations/signs.
workedExample: Survey questions about similar behaviors may load on a small number of latent traits.
